summary: The narrator, fleeing through Los Angeles after leaving a half-drunk bottle with fingerprints and DNA at a grocery store, weighs the risk of being identified and linked to earlier killings, including the deaths of Korean kids at Tresting's office and Rio's massacre of office workers. He decides to go back for the bottles, but finds the area swarming with police cars and a helicopter overhead. Trapped between dumpsters with his escape routes cut off, he considers grenades and violence as Plan B while searching for a better Plan A, reflecting that he rarely targets law enforcement.
one_line: A fugitive narrator, trapped in a Los Angeles alley by police cars and a helicopter, weighs going back for forensic evidence he left at a grocery store.
key_facts: The narrator left a half-drunk bottle of alcohol at a grocery store that carried his fingerprints and DNA.
The narrator worries that the forensic evidence could put him in the system and link him to the deaths of the Korean kids at Tresting's office.
The narrator also fears the evidence could link him to Rio's massacre of the office workers.
The narrator's information may already be in the system from the incident at Arthur's office.
The narrator decides to go back to the grocery store to grab the bottles because the consequences could be serious.
Three police cars screech into the alley behind the narrator, cutting off his escape route along the ground.
A helicopter's low thrum builds steadily, indicating a police air presence overhead.
The narrator slips between two dumpsters to hide from the police cars.
The narrator considers his grenades as a way to create enough chaos to escape.
The narrator labels blasting and shooting his way out as Plan B and says he needs a Plan A.
The narrator notes that law enforcement has never seemed like fair game as targets to him.
The narrator says most of his violent encounters did not occur on busy downtown streets with innocent bystanders.
The narrator has previously done no more than kick the odd uniform in the head while escaping police.
